gaps: The palette is a known warm-sepia fantasy register, safe rather than surprising
The title lockup's flare and glow treatment is the most conventional frame in the sequence
The map frame is flatter in light and depth than the mechanical close-ups, so it is a slight dip in density

tells: A systemic broadcast package: the '26' numeral is extruded into a relief architecture that each nation re-skins (Mexico, Argentina, Germany), which is a real design system rather than one layout with the words swapped

Studio watermark plus consistent finish across many variants suggests high-volume, high-craft sports broadcast work
gaps: The idea stays at network-branding level: flags plus the '26' mark plus players. It is strong execution of a brief, but it has no surprising conceit like B's clockwork world

The player-hero frame falls back on the stock sports-graphics template (cut-out, stacked name, swoosh), which weakens the otherwise distinctive relief system

tells: Dense, layered material work: translucent jelly hand, coral sponge growth, glass-and-amber organic sculpture, crumpled fabric and fibrous threads, all with believable subsurface scattering and caustics
Deliberate, unusual palettes that change frame to frame (dusty rose over volcanic black, saturated sky blue, sage green with chartreuse cloth, bottle green with ice-mint glass) yet read as one system
Real light: rim light on the terrain, backlit glass refraction, volumetric glow from the eruption plume
Variety of scale and camera across frames (macro detail, wide landscape, hero object against horizon) suggests real choreography rather than one repeated layout
Typography is minimal: a bold grotesk wordmark set in a corner plus a stencil/geometric 'OFFF MX' logo. It does the job as a festival/studio-ident tag, but it is not where the ideas are
gaps: There is no single unifying concept the way B's living map has one. It reads as a gorgeous collection of material studies rather than a story with a beginning and end; it needs a through-line (a transformation, or one object evolving)

The type is an afterthought: small default-ish bold sans labels dropped into corners. Integrate the names into the material world (grown, extruded, refracted) the way B forges its title into the astrolabe
There is no structural payoff or resolve frame. Build to a final lock-up that the preceding frames are clearly constructing toward

tells: A specific, ownable idea: the world itself as a clockwork map, with cities that mechanically assemble out of the terrain. Nobody else's show could have this title
Tactile, physical materials: tooled leather and bronze armillary band with relief engraving, wood, brass gears, aged-parchment map with hand-drawn rivers
Light is motivated by the story: a central sun blasts through the astrolabe, and low raking light picks out the miniature architecture with shallow depth of field
Typography has a clear point of view: an engraved Trajan-like serif with sigil ornaments, small-caps credits tucked into the world, and a title lock-up forged into the metal band
The frames choreograph a journey: overhead map to low tracking shots of mechanisms unfolding to the bookend resolve on the sun-ring. Every frame is a poster
gaps: The palette leans heavily on warm sepia and bronze throughout. A slightly bolder colour accent for each region could add rhythm
The credits are small and sometimes compete with busy mechanical detail (the Michelle Fairley card). The hierarchy could be tightened
The final lock-up glow is close to a conventional epic-title bloom. That moment of the piece takes the least risk

tells: A coherent broadcast system built around an extruded, layered '26' glyph that becomes architecture, a tunnel and a frame for each nation

Typography adapts to each nation: chunky italic 3D for ARGENTINA, a custom ornamental blackletter-adjacent hand-drawn lettering with folk-pattern filigree for DIE NATIONALELF, and stacked repeat type behind Vinícius
Flag colours are used as structural planes rather than flat fills; there is genuine dimensional depth, bevels and paper-cut layering
Player cut-out composites, cloth simulation on the flag and the brand lock-up resolve show a full sports-package workflow
gaps: The palette is dictated entirely by flags and the client, and the frames get busy and loud. The idea serves the brand more than it surprises; it needs one image that transcends sports-package convention
The player frame falls into generic sports-graphics clutter (cut-out + flag + logo + repeat type). Hold back and give it the restraint and single-image clarity of B's best frames
The materials are clean CG with little real texture or atmospheric light. Add physical grain, weathering or motivated lighting to give it B's tactility

tells: A clear system: the '26' numeral is extruded into deep, layered relief tunnels and reworked in each nation's flag colours (Mexico, Argentina, the red end card), so it reads as one broadcast package and not a set of separate slides

Each nation gets its own graphic language. Germany uses a hand-lettered 'DIE NATIONALELF' in red and gold baroque ornament on a black, fabric-like ground, and Argentina has the sun emblem with Vamos-pattern surf tiles. These are specific design decisions
Real material and light: bevelled paper or plaster relief, ambient occlusion in the tunnel recesses, cloth texture on the German frame

Frames vary in scale and camera (flat graphic, 3D tunnel, portrait), which points to choreographed transitions
gaps: The type is mostly stock heavy italic sports sans with bevels and drop shadows (VINÍCIUS JÚNIOR, ARGENTINA). Only Germany shows a real typographic idea, so bring that custom-lettering approach to every nation

Brand marks crowd the frames (FOX bug, FIFA, trophy). Cut down to fewer, more confident poster moments with more negative space and a single hierarchy

tells: A specific, memorable idea that only this piece could have: the world is a clockwork map that builds itself, so geography becomes mechanism and the title sequence becomes the show's political atlas
An engraved astrolabe band with dragon reliefs, lit from behind by a blown-out sun. The gold-and-sepia palette is warm and deliberate
Physical miniature textures (wood, brass, bone, parchment map) with shallow depth of field and directional light, so every frame works as a poster
Restrained, well-chosen type: a Trajan-like engraved serif with a sigil marker for each credit, sitting quietly inside the image. The title lockup is set into the astrolabe band
Clear choreography: a sun-flare opening, then crane moves over the rising cities, then the map, then a return to the astrolabe for the title. The structure is circular
gaps: Small credits shrink at small sizes and against busy miniatures. A bit more contrast or tracking would help them read
The bookend title card is close to a conventional emblem lockup, less surprising than the mechanical cities
The palette is almost all sepia and gold, which leaves little colour contrast between locations

tells: Dense, tactile 3D with a clear material language: translucent glassy hands, a coral-like heart, fabric folds, mesh, fibre and hair simulation, chrome tubes. This is real look-dev, not stock primitives
The palette is unusual and changes in a controlled way: dusty pink and rust, a violet dusk, a clean blue sky, sage and blush, bottle green with glacial blue
Each frame is a different environment yet still feels like one organic or synthetic world. The credit names (Boldtron, Medusa Lab, OFFF MX) fit a festival-titles format with many contributors
Light is motivated: a rim-lit glass figure against a gradient horizon, and an erupting peak lit from within
gaps: The type is a plain bold grotesk dropped into the upper left like a lower-third credit. It needs a typographic idea tied to the forms, the way B builds its credits in
The idea is mostly about texture ('strange organic matter'). It lacks B's narrative or metaphorical spine, so the frames could be shuffled
The OFFF logo is laid flat on a busy image instead of being staged, which weakens the payoff

defects: No strip files were supplied, so the motion read comes only from the 6 sampled frames and the 3 pairs; easing and overlap could not be checked frame by frame

Northbridge → Harbour transition is a plain cross-dissolve with both cards ghosted: the lighthouse and 'HARBOUR' bleed through the red bridge card at mid-opacity, which looks muddy rather than designed
The propeller-like X shadow over the ball at the centre spot is repeated in two shots and reads as a stock blurred-shadow effect, not a motivated object
The split-pitch frame crops 'NORTHBRIDGE' off the left edge and has both club colours dissolving over a soft-focus half; the type is blurred and the frame sits between states
The final scoreboard frame crops '19:4' so the payoff number is cut off; the hold reads as an unfinished push-in
Per-second change falls to 6.4 at about 6s: a near-static hold with no reason in an already slow piece; the longest shot is 4.0s against a ~1.0s benchmark
Opening floodlight shot is mostly black, with rain as the only motion; dead air before the idea starts
Uniform mid-tone grain at 100%, with no clear light interaction on the type; the type is clean but flat and has no edge glow or bloom where the floodlight theme invites it
gaps: Choreography and transitions: shots hand off by dissolves and slow pushes instead of built match-cuts. The bulbs, ball and centre circle could drive every transition (the ball hits the centre spot and the bridge arc becomes the circle; floodlight bulbs become the scoreboard dots), with proper easing and impact. The energy peak comes at about 45%, then dips, and never builds to a real climax before the 19:45 reveal

Sound is generated noise design only: four click transients, two noise risers, two filtered sweeps and a sub drone, with no tonal partials, no crowd, no stadium bed and no musical arrangement. The dynamics are risers into hard cuts with no layered hit on the reveal; the loudness target is met, but the sound is thin compared with produced sports-promo audio

Finish and framing: several frames would not work as posters (black opener, cropped final numerals, ghosted dissolves). Light is painted rather than lit; it needs real bloom and falloff on the bulbs, interaction between the floodlights and the type, and a locked final lockup that settles fully on 19:45 with both crests
